newsitem.title: UK: UK OFT says rights issues underwriters face MMC.
newsitem.headline: UK OFT says rights issues underwriters face MMC.

text.p: Britain's director general of fair trading John Bridgeman said on Wednesday he was not satisfied there was sufficient commitment to open up the market for the underwriting of rights issues to competition.

"It is now up to the industry to decide whether to reform without such a reference or to subject itself to the full rigours of the MMC (Monopolies and Mergers Commission). I am not prepared to wait much longer for real and sustained evidence of a change," he said.

At a conference on new forms of corporate finance, Bridgeman called for greater use of alternatives to underwriting -- where there has been a generally accepted standard charge of two percent of the capital raised by the underwriting financier -- such as deep discounting and bookbuilding.

Financial advisers had traditionally advised an underwritten issue at a discount of between 10 and 15 percent below a company's current market price if the firm concerned wanted to raise capital by issuing equity, he said.
But having recommended a rights issue, the adviser could then go on to act as both underwriter and broker for the issue, creating a "clear potential conflict of interest", Bridgeman said.

"In these circumstances it is difficult to see financial advisers recommending a non-underwritten rights issue at a deep discount from the prevailing market price, although this appears to be the cheapest method of raising capital from an equity issue," he added.
